subject: [PATCH v2 0/8] nfsd/sunrpc: harden the netlink listener interfaces

reviews.author: Chuck Lever
reviews.summary: reviewer noted that the fixture leaks the network namespace for tests that finish with a listener still up, and suggested adding code in FIXTURE_TEARDOWN() to drop any services created by the test

reviews.author: Chuck Lever
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that for an IPv4 listener, the port-zero callback falls back to __svc_rpcb_register4(), which can remove mappings for existing listeners on other transports if PMAPPROC_UNSET is used and its protocol argument is ignored.
reviews.raw_body:
For an IPv4 listener, the port-zero callback falls back through
__svc_rpcb_register4() to rpcb_register(). PMAPPROC_UNSET ignores
its protocol argument, so unwinding a partially successful TCP
registration also removes the mappings for existing listeners on
other transports, I would think.

It might be that the best the kernel can do here is tear everything
down if one registration fails.


-- 
Chuck Lever

2026-08-11.patch_summary: This patch set hardens the netlink listener interfaces in the NFS daemon (nfsd) and SunRPC code by addressing several issues that were causing stalls and hangs. The changes include rejecting invalid transport names, capping the number of listener_set requests at 1024 entries, improving error handling for registration failures, and bounding the local rpcbind client to a single attempt. Additionally, the patch set includes tests for listener creation failures and a per-netns rpcbind stub. While this patch set improves performance and reduces stalls, it does not address the root cause of the issues, which is the synchronous nature of rpcbind calls. A separate patchset is planned to make these calls asynchronous.

reviews.author: Jeff Layton (author)
reviews.summary: The author is addressing concerns about how to handle rpcbind registration errors in NFSv2/3, specifically whether the listener set netlink call should wait for registration to complete or declare reg errors as non-fatal and leave cleanup to the admin. The author proposes two alternatives: blocking longer to try unregistering things if they fail, or declaring reg errors as non-fatal with a pr_warn() and leaving it up to the admin to clean up.
reviews.raw_body:
What I was thinking for NFSv2/3 was to just have the listener set
netlink call wait for registration to complete before returning to
userland. That would mean we'd have to block even longer to try and
unregister things if things fail.

Alternate proposal: let's just declare rpcbind reg errors to be non-
fatal: do a pr_warn() and just leave it up to the admin to sort it out
if that happens instead of trying to fail the startup.

The resulting situation for the server is no worse off (it's just
running instead of being down), and I move that we're better off
leaving it up to a human to clean up the mess instead of trying to fix
things up from the kernel.

Thoughts?
-- 
Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>

reviews.author: Chuck Lever
reviews.summary: Reviewer suggested that the kernel should fail back to the previous configuration if it cannot set the requested configuration, and also proposed handling rpcbind registration from user space instead of the kernel.
reviews.raw_body:
I was thinking of this in terms of a declarative administrative UI:
If the kernel can't set the requested configuration, it should
fail back to the previous configuration. Maybe that's not possible.

On the other hand, what might be better is to handle the rpcbind
registration from user space instead of the kernel, after the
kernel listener is set up.


-- 
Chuck Lever

reviews.author: Jeff Layton (author)
reviews.summary:
Author acknowledges that making netlink interfaces behave like /proc ones will be difficult, but doesn't commit to a fix or further revision.

Author acknowledges that making the rpcbind registration non-fatal is still the best solution, but expresses concerns about fundamentally changing the interface and dealing with legacy cases.
reviews.raw_body:
It's possible, but difficult. The original /proc interfaces were never
this clean, so making the underlying bits behave this way for the
netlink interfaces, but not the legacy /proc ones will be hard.

Also, today we don't take any steps to try and preserve the old
listener table. That would have to be done here as well.

---

That's possible I guess. We could send a new boolean down in the
listener call that says "don't do any rpcbind registration" and then if
the kernel indicates that it understands that message then userland
could do the registration.

That's a major undertaking though and I don't like fundamentally
changing the interface here, particularly when we'll still have to cope
with doing this from the kernel for legacy cases.

I still think the best solution of all would be to just say
"henceforth, rpcbind registration is non-fatal". That just leaves the
kernel succeeding the listener set today when it would have failed
before, but will still printk() an appropriate warning in that case, so
the admin should be aware that rpcbind registration failed, even though
the server is up.

Right now, I'm really unclear on what sort of changes you want to see
here as a final patchset. What would make this mergeable for you?
-- 
Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>

reviews.author: Chuck Lever
reviews.summary: Reviewer Chuck Lever requested changes to patches 4, 6, and 8, including making registration failure non-fatal for NFSv2 and NFSv3, extending the extack in patch 6 to report a listener that came up without registering, fixing a netns leak in patch 8, and moving tests that assert unwind or abort to the new failure policy.
reviews.raw_body:
Sorry for the ambiguity. For the re-roll:

- 1, 2, 3 and 5 don't need change.

- Let's drop patch 4/8.

- Make registration failure non-fatal for NFSv2 and NFSv3, as
  proposed.
  
- Extend the extack in 6/8 to report a listener that came up without
  registering. dmesg is the only channel write_ports() has. Perhaps
  the netlink path can do better?

- Fix the netns leak in 8/8.

- Ensure that any test that asserts the unwind or the abort is moved
  over to the new failure policy.

HTH.

-- 
Chuck Lever
